characterization_methods.key_findings: Rheological stress is primarily influenced by T and ε̇; the steel is a negative temperature-sensitive and positive strain rate-sensitive material — rheological stress decreases with decreasing ε̇ or increasing T.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: T = 900–1150 °C (this sample at 1150 °C); strain rates 0.01, 0.1, 1 and 10 s^-1 (this sample at 0.1 s^-1); maximum compression 60% (true strain 0.92); cylindrical specimen F 8 mm × 12 mm.
characterization_methods.purpose: Obtain rheological (flow) stress curves and study the hot deformation behavior / DRX of the steel.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: LEXT OLS4000 laser confocal microscope; etchant 30% nitric acid alcohol solution (volume fraction)
characterization_methods.key_findings: Reveals the initial large polygonal grain structure with segregation striations and, after compression, the zone-dependent DRX morphologies (difficult / small / large deformation zones).
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Compressed sample split in half along the axial axis, then prepared, ground, polished and etched; micrographs taken with 100 µm scale bars.
characterization_methods.purpose: Collect microstructure images to analyze the microstructure evolution and deformation zones of the steel.

analytical_models.equation_role: Relate peak stress, temperature and strain rate; determine dynamic recrystallization activation energy Qp via Qp = 1000·R·k1·k2.
analytical_models.model_name: Arrhenius hyperbolic sine equation (Eq. 1) / activation-energy Eq. 2
analytical_models.model_note: Computed from the whole experimental matrix (T=900–1150 °C, ε̇=0.01–10 s^-1); the fitted lines are not parallel, so Qp is only the average activation energy over the experimental range.

parameters.name: k1 (average slope of ln ε̇ vs ln[sinh(ασp)], Fig. 4a)
k2 (average slope of ln[sinh(ασp)] vs 1000/T, Fig. 4b)

computational_details.simulation_method: Arrhenius-type hyperbolic sine constitutive analysis (linear regression of ln ε̇ vs ln[sinh(ασp)] and ln[sinh(ασp)] vs 1000/T)

analytical_models.equation_role: Temperature-compensated strain rate to characterise the combined influence of T and ε̇ on rheological stress.
analytical_models.model_note: lnZ values for the full matrix are tabulated in Table 1; for this sample (0.1 s^-1, 1150 °C) the value is 54.32. lnZ increases with increasing ε̇ or decreasing T.

parameters.name: lnZ at T = 1150 °C and ε̇ = 0.1 s^-1 (this sample)

computational_details.simulation_method: Zener-Hollomon parameter calculation (Eq. 3: Z = ε̇ exp(Qp/RT))

analytical_models.equation_role: Describe the normalized flow curve and determine the material constant C from the slope of ln(σ/σp) vs [ln(ε/εp)+1-ε/εp].
analytical_models.model_note: Fit for C at 1050 °C/0.01 s^-1 gives C = 0.1461 with R = 0.9728 (Fig. 5); C under other T and ε̇ obtained by the same method.

analytical_models.equation_role: Relate critical strain to peak strain via εc/εp = [√(1-C) - (1-C)]/C.
analytical_models.model_note: Result consistent with literature using the θ-σ inflection point to identify DRX critical strain.

computational_details.simulation_method: Cingara-McQueen equation with Poliak-Jonas inflection criterion for critical strain

analytical_models.equation_role: Give critical, peak and steady-state strain/stress as functions of lnZ for the steel.
analytical_models.model_note: Regression fits of the six characteristic values against lnZ with correlation coefficients R between 0.911 and 0.957 (Fig. 6); with increasing lnZ the initiation and completion of DRX become more difficult.

computational_details.simulation_method: Multiple linear regression fitting of flow-stress characteristic values against lnZ

analytical_models.equation_role: Express DRX average grain size drex as a function of initial grain size, strain, strain rate and temperature.
analytical_models.model_note: a, h, p, q and b are parameters to be determined; d0 is the initial grain size.

analytical_models.equation_role: Fitted prediction of DRX average grain size (µm) for the low-density high-strength steel.
analytical_models.model_name: Fitted DRX average grain size model (Eq. 12)

parameters.name: Q in exp(-Q/RT)
parameters.unit: J mol^-1 (as used with R and T)

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Billet set as a rigid-plastic body and the die indenter as a rigid body; material parameters given to the die; a semi-symmetric specimen used as the deformation model; friction of the contact interface between billet and die set to shear type with value 0.3; convection coefficient of billet and air set as 0.02 N/(s·mm·°C); initial grain size and strain treated as fixed values.
computational_details.simulation_method: Finite element simulation of hot compression and regression of DRX average grain size (Levenberg-Marquardt optimisation)
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Correlation coefficient R = 0.996 and average relative error MRE = 4.53% for all samples; absolute error between predicted and experimental grain size mostly within 3 µm (Fig. 11).

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The cylindrical sample was heated to 1200 °C at a rate of 10 °C/s (first segment of the Gleeble-3500 schedule).
Homogenized by holding at 1200 °C for 120 s.
Cooled from 1200 °C to the set deformation temperature of 1150 °C at a rate of 5 °C/s.
Held at the set temperature (1150 °C) for 15 s before compression so that the temperature difference between the inside and outside of the sample was the same.

Isothermal constant-strain-rate compression to a maximum compression of 60% (true strain 0.92) at a constant strain rate of 0.1 s^-1, carried out on a Gleeble-3500 thermo-mechanical simulator. Mica foils with high-temperature lubricants were affixed to both end faces to reduce friction and deformation non-uniformity.
After compression, the sample was sprayed with water to cool the steel down.

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: Large polygonal grains; individual grains span roughly one to a few times the length of the 100 µm scale bar; no numeric grain size is printed on the figure.

structures.overall_structure: Initial (pre-deformation, as-forged) microstructure of the Fe-Mn-Al-C steel: large polygonal grains delimited by bright, continuous, slightly etched boundaries enclosing dark grey grain interiors. Within essentially every grain the interior carries many fine, closely spaced, parallel light-grey striations/lamellae whose direction changes from grain to grain, giving a strongly banded, dendritic/interdendritic segregation contrast rather than a uniform solid solution, indicating chemical heterogeneity in the as-forged condition. This is the starting state before the 1150 °C/0.1 s^-1 compression.

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: Highest degree of DRX among the three zones; equiaxed recrystallized grains, becoming increasingly uniform as T increases and strain rate decreases; grain size increases with decreasing strain rate or increasing T (coarse grains at high T / low strain rate).

microstructure_list.region: large deformation zone (zone 3 / core of compressed sample)

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: Intermediate degree of DRX, between zone 3 and zone 1.
Lowest degree of DRX; coarse equiaxed grains with straight, annealing-twin-like boundaries persist.

microstructure_list.region: difficult deformation zone (zone 1, near loading surfaces)

structures.overall_structure: Dynamic recrystallization (DRX) morphology of the hot-compressed Fe-Mn-Al-C steel. During hot deformation the grain boundaries of the elongated original grains become serrated and small equiaxed DRX grains decorate the elongated original grain boundaries in a 'necklace' arrangement at high strain rate (10 s^-1); with decreasing strain rate the recrystallized grains grow and the microstructure homogeneity improves. The degree of DRX follows: large-deformation zone (3) > small-deformation zone (2) > difficult-deformation zone (1). With increasing T the volume fraction of DRX increases (at 1050 °C DRX is basically completed within the large-deformation zone), and the recrystallized grain size grows markedly with increasing T and decreasing strain rate.

unmapped_findings: The sample-specific peak stress at 1150 °C/0.1 s^-1 is not numerically reported. The text gives peak-stress values only for other strain rates: at 0.01 s^-1 peak stress falls from 305.4 MPa at 900 °C to 53.8 MPa at 1150 °C (82% reduction); at 10 s^-1 the reduction is 73% over the same temperature range (b0024).

The DRX average grain size for this exact sample condition (1150 °C, 0.1 s^-1) is not numerically reported. Fig. 10 (figure_010) shows that at 1150 °C the 0.01 s^-1 curve reaches just below 80 µm while the 10 s^-1 curve stays near 25 µm; the 0.1 s^-1 curve lies between these.
For the steel, at 1150 °C and 0.01 s^-1 the DRX grain size exceeds 70 µm, giving a coarse-grain structure (b0063).

Recommended hot-working window for a fine and uniform grain structure: 950–1000 °C/0.01–0.1 s^-1 and 1050–1100 °C/1–10 s^-1 (b0065, b0012, b0086). This sample (1150 °C/0.1 s^-1) lies outside this optimum window (high T + low-to-intermediate strain rate gives coarse grains).

The steel is a negative temperature-sensitive and positive strain rate-sensitive material; the rheological stress increases with increasing ε̇ or decreasing T, and the peak stress can be reduced by decreasing ε̇ or increasing T (b0024, b0084).
The lnZ for this sample (0.1 s^-1, 1150 °C) is 54.32 (Table 1); the extreme lnZ entries of the table are 70.99 (10 s^-1, 900 °C) and 52.01 (0.01 s^-1, 1150 °C).

The same Fe-Mn-Al-C steel batch with the same composition was tested under identical experimental conditions to confirm the reproducibility of the results; the reported experimental phenomena are stated to be reproducible (b0018, b0024, b0037, b0058, b0065).
Material composition (mass fraction, %): 1.46 C, 25.14 Mn, 10 Al, 0.053 Nb, balance Fe; the forging billet was machined into a cylindrical specimen of F 8 mm × 12 mm (b0018).
Dynamic recrystallization activation energy of the steel = 669.844 kJ mol^-1, determined as an average over the experimental range because the fitted lines in Fig. 4 are not parallel (b0032, b0085).
